136325.overview:
Speed Racer is a racing game, played from a third-person perspective, similar to Pole Position. The aim of the game is to pass a specific number of cars during each lap of a race. Success allows the player to continue with the next lap while failure will lead to game over. To win a race, five laps have to be completed and each lap is two miles long. Controls are basic and limited to steering, accelerating and braking. The shoulder of the road should be avoided since driving on it for too long will lead to the car stopping. A repair crew will then appear and put on new tires. The game consists of four different race tracks that can be played in any order.
The game was created by Steven Hirsch for MichTron.

136427.overview:
This is a Miner clone, consisting of 35 screens. You get five lives plus a bonus life at 5,000 points. Features include moving and collapsing platforms, electric walls, transporters, moving beams, switches, and everyday objects turned mutant such as screws, televisions and scissors. Monsters, screws, scissors and even food will impede your passage through this multi-screen game. Our hero must negotiate his way through the 35 complex screens, collecting the key to the next level on the way. There are numerous traps and monsters to hinder your progress, which include icicles, screws, drinks, food, scissors, electric walls, moving platforms, collapsing floors, balls, conveyor belts and many more. 

By skilfull use of the platforms, walkways and the switches you might survive to level 34, then you have the challenge of the penultimate last level - only the experts will make it.

137255.overview:
Released by Microdeal as Skramble, this is a pretty accurate remake of the arcade game Scramble.

You fly your craft across a horizontally scrolling landscape, and the objective of the game is to stay alive while scoring points by destroying enemy missiles, fuel depots, mystery bases, and so on. Your craft is equipped with a gun and bombs. Destroy enemy fuel depots to get more fuel for your craft before you run out and crash.
The landscape scrolls at a constant speed. It is possible to temporary speed up or slow down your jet, but you have to stay within the screen.
There are five stages in this game and completing all stages brings you back to the start of the game. 

The Mountains:
You fly over mountains bombing and shooting enemy objects located on the ground. Watch out for missiles that are fired at your craft.
The UFO cave:
You fly through a cave filled with UFOs. Shoot or avoid the UFOs and bomb the objects on the ground. Luckily, no missiles will be fired in this level.
The Fireballs:
You continue through the cave, but now you have to dodge indestructible fireballs. Remember to drop those bombs on ground objects.
The City:
Similar to the mountains except that the landscape is different. Enemy objects are often well protected inside silos.
The Maze:
Fly your ship through a maze of narrow passages all the way to the enemy base.

162215.overview:
Strategic Command is a strategy game for two players that is played on a map with five islands. Each player has three bases which produce units: an army base, a naval base and a capital. The army and naval bases can only produce their own kind of units while the capital can produce both. To win the game a player has to take control of the capital of the enemy.

There are sixteen types of units and they are deployed in task forces of up to three units. Task forces can then be moved around the screen and when getting close to an enemy combat will occur. Each unit has an attacking factor and a defensive factor. Each attack will cause the defensive factor of the target to decrease with the attacking factor of the attacker. When it reaches zero the unit is destroyed. Additionally players can lay mines through special units that will be completely destroy the unit stepping on to that tile.

175417.overview: The Dragon or Tandy Coco never received an official conversion of Boulder Dash, but they did receive one or two home-grown clones. Stone Raider II has all the features of the original, with the fast enemies, the digging, the falling stones and the set amount of crystals that must be collected to open the exit. A particular enemy is the slime, which multiplies to fill all open space, and is dangerous both to the player and other enemies. There are 25 levels to complete. Except for being published by MicroDeal as well, there is no relationship to the original Stone Raider (later re-released as Stone Raider II), also based on Boulder Dash, but different.

175421.overview:
Shock Trooper is a refined arcade adventure where you, as a fifth column shocktrooper, must infiltrate an alien base and free your captive mates. The complex has a very strong radiation field, which means you must keep on moving unless you want to die just from ambient radiation.

You carry a beam weapon, whose beam can extend across the entire screen. The longer you fire it, though, you expose yourself to more radiation. Use the weapon to destroy turrets and power generators which sustain force fields which block your way. Different hostile creatures will also patrol the complex and try to kill you. At certain locations, you are unable to use your gun. Beside that, the main component of the game is to use the platforms and lifts to get to the right place where you can shut off a generator so that you can reach the next generator whose forcefield shuts your path to your mates off.

At the end of each level, the radiation you have absorbed is removed, and you receive one of the aliens' secret TRG-5 attack saucer sub-assemblies which must be brought back to your allies.

175422.overview: The player controls a spaceship which moves in all directions, and can fire vertically upwards or downwards. Gameplay takes place within a series of nebula which can not be shot through. Each level has a red ship that wanders randomly off the screen, multiple blue ships that encircle a vortex, a large planet with a single benign ship attached to it, and 3 green saucers that fly about at random. The goal for each level is to destroy all enemy vessels, and when this is accomplished, the player progresses to another identical level. The player's is tasked with protecting the city on each level, but only one structure can actually be destroyed, and the enemy AI prevents the other buildings from ever being hit, making the entire issue of city defense moot. The player starts with 3 ships, but gains an addition ship when a level is completed. If all ships are lost, it's game over.

175424.overview:
Syzygy is a 1-player 1st person text adventure for the Dragon 32/64.

You are trapped aboard a section of the Deathstar. You have had a near fatal encounter with the Dark Lord Vader, and your strength is all but gone. Furthermore, you know that Vader is somewhere near. You may not be able to destroy him, but he guards a computer which holds information that you desperately need. To have any chance against the Dark Lord, you must get your Light Saber, which you lost in the previous duel.

Player from a 1st person perspective, the player must navigate the hallways of the Deathstar. Numerous dangers can cause instant death. The player must outsmart a Huge Ugly Alien, penetrate the vault of the Death Star, recover their lost communicator, and solve a number of other dangers. All commands are via VERB NOUN entry. The player's inventory is displayed on the screen at all times, and there is a save and restore feature. Features arcade lightsaber duels with Darth Vader.

175430.overview:
Storm is a clone of Atari's arcade hit, Tempest, but whereas that game used sharp vector graphics, this version is rendered in blocky text graphics.

You control a ship moving along the edge of a tunnel-like construction. From the far end of the tunnel come coloured bars of various colours. Moving around the tunnel's mouth, you shoot the bars until you reach a set score, which will promote you to the next level. With only 99 shots granted on each level, it is better to let the bars reach the end of the tunnel than to miss them with your gun. One kind of bar that should not be missed, though, is the orange kind, called ”Millibars”. These will, if they reach the edge of the tunnel, chase you around. After a while, the Millibars will disappear, but if more than one has reached the edge where you are, avoiding them long enough can be very difficult. The game becomes gradually more difficult as you progress through the levels, and on later levels, the tunnel itself is no longer shown.

175431.overview: This is a maze game heavily inspired by Pac Man but not quite delivering on the ambition... You run around a maze eating yellow dots while avoiding the red ghosts. Eat a power pellet and the ghosts turn blue for a while. During this period the ghosts can be chased down and eaten for additional points.

175516.overview: St George and the Dragons is a single screen action game where the player controls the saint. A wizard has imprisoned a number of maidens in an enchanted castle and it's up to George to free them. The spell of the castle is tied to a rock and to free the maidens George has to use his sword to cleave the rock. The rock is located in the bottom left corner of the screen and to reach it George must use a bridge to cross a river. At the same time it's necessary to avoid or kill the fire breathing dragon that is hunting the hero. Getting hit by the dragon's fire or running into the water leads to a life being lost. Once the rock has been hit by the sword the level is completed and the player earns one point and moves on to another level which works exactly the same way.

175714.overview:
The Sword and the Sorcerer is a dungeon crawler set in a maze consisting of 225 locations that the player has to explore, one screen at a time, with the aim of making it out in one piece. To succeed with that it's necessary to collect three pieces of a key and to locate a bolted door to escape through. In the maze the player will come across more or less dangerous creatures (there are nineteen in total) and he will also find weapons (thirteen different ones), gold, potions and food.

The game is entirely controlled with the keyboard and all actions are available from a menu and the player has to enter the corresponding number. To get past a creature the player either has to attack it, bribe it or trade with it. For each attack the enemy and the player will lose some strength and the player has to keep entering the command until the enemy has died. If losing the player can choose to run away but it will cost five strength points. Strength is also decreased by one for every move made in the maze but it's possible to recharge it by eating food or drinking potions. The player has an inventory for eight items and of those one offensive and one defensive weapon can be equipped. Different weapons do different damage on different enemies.

175765.overview: The legend goes that once upon a time a sultan was visiting the maze in Hampton Court. There he was robbed his jewels by a group of thieves, and his brave bodyguard entered the maze to recover them, only to be murdered by the thieves on his way back. In present day, the player is an adventurer who accepts the mission to explore the maze and recover the jewels. The maze is shown in a 1st person view, and the player has to navigate it in order to find the jewels and take them outside. Apart from getting lost and exhaustion, other dangers await him, especially in the shape the ghost of the Sultan's bodyguard, who still haunts the place. Sultan's Maze is a primitive 3D adventure well known to enthusiasts of the Amstrad CPC; in many countries it was part of the free game pack that accompanied the computer.

175766.overview:
Wiping the sweat from my brow, I searched the inky blackness ahead for signs of enemy fighters. Though Star Jammer was the best ship in the galaxy, my dwindling energy reserves made me doubt I could reach the next stargate. Suddenly something registered on my scanners...

Star Jammer is a one player arcade game requiring 1 joystick.

175782.overview: In Super Spy a jet fighter carrying a nuclear warhead has disappeared under mysterious circumstances while out on a training exercise and no wreckage has been found. The player has been summoned by the Spy Master and given a mission to find the jet fighter and defuse the deadly cargo. Super Spy starts as a text adventure game in which the player is a James Bond style character who has to negotiate their way past the people and the puzzles to achieve the objectives. Once the players has found their way far enough the game changes into a 3D graphic maze for the player to find their way to the goal and complete the mission.

175803.overview: The player is situated in the cockpit of the Columbia space shuttle. The player has 3 landings options, starting from orbit, entering the atmosphere, or a short distance from the runway. Player can control the shuttle's thrusters in space, and as they go below 58 miles altitude can control the pitch, roll, yaw, speedbrakes, and landing gear of their vessel. Time progresses in 10 second intervals as the player manually enters corrections for their craft. The player must be careful controlling their descent through the atmosphere to avoid burning up or deflecting off into space. The player must line up the runway and ensure they land safely. The current altitude, speed, heading, position, and temperature of their aircraft is displayed on the screen.

175940.overview:
In Shenanigans players are looking for the Leprechaun’s proverbial pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. The adventure begins, of all places, in the protagonist's own modest bedroom apartment. From that point players will need to roam the streets and interact with other people during their adventure. They will explore woods, caves, and, of course, encounter a leprechaun along the way. But remember, the prize is that pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.

This graphical interactive fiction game uses standard single letter direction (N, S, E, W) for movement. Players can also SAVE their current location on cassette for restarting later. The command parser is a standard verb noun system (eg, "Go Door").

177518.overview: In this text adventure, you play the friend of a professor who has gone missing on some kind of archaeological survey. Your task is to find the professor, or at least to find out of his fate. On your adventure, you will ride the taxi a lot (and must find a way to pay the driver), travel by airplane and visit a remote, mysterious island. The command interpreter is of a rather simple verb-noun mould, with some peculiarities such as SAYing your wishes to the taxi driver.

198025.overview: Storm Arrows is a variant of the arcade game Targ. The game takes place in grid-like network of streets where the player drives a land skimmer. The player is pursued by a group of seven imperial storm arrows who attempt to crash into the player. To complete a level all of the storm arrows have to be destroyed. Additionally there are imperial pursuit cruisers that lay contact mines on the street. If not destroyed these mines will turn into new storm arrows when there is only one storm arrow left on the screen. The skimmer is equipped with a limited number of torpedoes and when running out it is necessary to get new ones from refuelling stations that appear randomly on the screen.

211063.overview:
Shark Treasure is a single screen action game where the player controls a diver who has to collect as many gold bars as possible. The gold is located on the sea floor and the player has to swim down and pick up the treasure before returning to the boat at the surface. This is made more complicated by the presence of huge sharks that swim back and forth across the screen and who will quickly eat any divers that get in their way. Thus they have to be avoided and to help the player is equipped with a limited supply of flash grenades which scare the sharks and cause them to turn around and swim in the opposite direction.

Only a total amount of three grenades and gold bars can be carried at a time and the player therefore has to make several dives to get all the gold. The game starts with two sharks in the water but there is one more added each time the sea floor is cleared of treasure.

Th game was originally released in 1982, it was once again released by Microdeal in 1985.

216932.overview:
You are the Starship Chameleon commissioned to protect your planet by intercepting the falling bombs launched by the enemy Gabolators from above. Beware, this is a dangerous mission! There are five types of bombs.

Bombs are destroyed by running the Starship into them. However, this is only effective if the Starship and the bomb are in the same state, i.e. matter (blue) or anti-matter (yellow). To switch the state of your Starship, press the fire button on the joystick. No matter what colour you are, red mines can destroy you. You begin the game with three Starships and you lose one every time you are destroyed. You are rewarded with an extra ship every 10,000 points.

217043.overview: You command the last combat viper and must break through the enemy fighters and the defenses of the death star to win. Beware the black hole as you manoeuvre your ship as its gravity pull can suck you in.  The death star has a defense shield with one weak spot in it. You must position yourself to fire a photon torpedo through it, whilst dodging defensive missiles from the death star. Invisible space mines can blow you apart, your only warning is a sonic alert just before they explode.

446520.overview: As a captain of SS Enterprise the player must defeat all the Klingon warships in the current quadrant in a designated time to save the empire. The ship is armed with phasers (energy weapon) and photon torpedoes (very limited, never miss the target). The player may use long and short range scanners. Using the shields requires diverting some energy level. Reaching the Starbase allows to refuel and rearm the ship plus replenish the energy cells. Most command activities drain the energy level. The impulse drive allows avoiding a collision with a star or Klingon's ship. Commands are given by pressing a certain key. If the ship runs out of the energy or the mission is not completed in the designated time, the mission fails.

446521.overview:
A word is displayed on the screen with blanks taking the place of letters. The player tries to guess the word by typing letters, but every incorrect guess adds a piece of a hangman to the screen. After 10 incorrect guesses, it's game over.

There are three levels of difficulty, and games can be timed or untimed. The player can miss three words before it's game over.

446522.overview:
Savage Island is the only multi-part game in Scott Adams' adventure series, all of which have a very similar parser and interface. At the completion of this game, players receive a password which allows part two to be played. The Savage Island games are also probably the most difficult adventures in the series!

The player begins trapped on a small remote island in the ocean, which is facing a hurricane and also has an active volcano. The player can cross a river, and will also need to explore a cave network. Items are often found by running through the sand with one's hands.

The island holds a great secret, which will not be discovered until both parts of the game have been completed.

446524.overview:
Shape Up is an educational game designed to teach young children to recognize shapes, it includes 5 short games:

Big and Small: Find the size of shape that corresponds to the one shown.
Build It: Construct a house by positioning shapes.
Burglar!: Find the shape that the burglar is stealing.
Find a Home: Find the house that corresponds to the shape shown.
Shunting: Find the corresponding shape.

446537.overview: Starfighter is a rather generic side-scrolling shoot'em'up with certain Scramble influences. Your plane travels across an undulating landscape where aliens sit at the ground. You can strafe down and shoot them on the ground, or wait until they lift off and fly into your line of sight. Your beam is short and thin, so precision is required in order to hit them before they fly into you. The game starts off in four-colour mode, then switches to black and white high resolution mode, possibly to simulate night flight. Three game speeds are available, and the screen scrolls fast, even at the slowest setting. Unlike the vast majority of games, it scrolls from left to right, instead of the opposite. Due to the use of analogue joysticks, and the speed of your ship, there is a lot of inertia in your control, which feels more realistic than the straight course in which you travel in other similar games.

446538.overview: Two identical martial artists face off against each other. Each match is timed for 60 seconds and, after each hit is landed, the combatants separate and restart the fight. The players gain more points for more accurate hits. The player with the most points after 60 seconds is the winner. The fighters can jump, flip, and throw a variety of punches and kicks.

446547.overview:
The player has seized vital documents from the enemy's headquarters after a daring raid. Unfortunately, the rescue helicopter was shot down, and the player is the only survivor. The player must reach Plato Bay by crossing nine minefields, while avoiding patrolling helicopter gunships and guards. The player starts with a mine detector and 10 percussion grenades.

Played from a top-down perspective, the player tries to cross the screen from the bottom to top. The mine detector will detect mines ahead, to the left, and right. Grenades can be used to knock out enemy bases, and these bases have wire-guided missiles to knock out patrolling helicopters. Extra grenades can be seized by passing through a minefield and surprising patrolling guards. There's a limited amount of daylight, and during night the player must maneuver using the metal detector and lights from the bases and patrolling guards.

446548.overview: Your mission is to go into space, survive an asteroid field before blasting alien ships, and if you allow any ships to escape then it is game over. Space Mission is a single screen shooter and your ship stays static in the middle of the screen but can turn in a 360 degree direction. As well as turn, your ship can also move forward in short bursts. Your ship can take so many hits from asteroids or alien ships' bullets and your damage status is told to you as it gets worse. Before you start the game you have a choice of seven skill levels from easy to suicidal.

446550.overview: The player controls Superkid, who can move laterally, and jump. The player attempts to jump over enemies including snails and snakes, and game play is divided into stages with progressively more difficult enemies. The player has limited time to complete each level. The player starts with 3 lives, and can pick up weapons during their adventure.

446562.overview: The player's mission is to take charge of the starship Endeavor, and destroy the aggressive fleet of Krugon Space Cruisers that have overrun the Universe. The ship is armed with 20 photon-guided missiles that can destroy any Krugon vessel, as well as Phasers and a number of starbases. The player moves their ship around a large space field that scrolls vertically and horizontally. The ship can rotate and move forwards. The player can dock with starbases to refuel and reenergize their vessel. Docking occurs from a 1st-person perspective. The player receives a performance index at the end of each game.

446563.overview:
In Eno, the player's eccentric aunt has just died and left the player her estate. She had millions. If the player finds it they can keep it. The only clue: living room. The player explores the rooms within his aunt's house looking for the treasure.

In Stalag, the player is alone in a Nazi prison camp, the year 1944. The Germans have moved all the other prisoners to a new camp as they know it is only a matter of hours until it is bombed by the Allies. They locked the gate and abandoned the camp, but the player was forgotten because they had been locked in the hot box. The player must escape the camp alive.

446569.overview:
Legend tells how long ago biomechanical beings from space called Flutter Drones attacked Earth to feed upon men's flesh. After a long battle, the people of Earth were able to drive them back, but the planet and its great cities were destroyed. Earth's people built one great city with a defense system against the drones. A network of towers, each with a scanner designed to seek and eradicate drone packs and air mines with minimum risk to human life, were created. Centuries have passed and only Scanner 13 remains standing, but the drones have come again. The player has entered the final scanner to try to protect the city from the incoming alien menace using the remnants of ancient technology.

The player's goal is to scan the entire city for the enemy presence and hidden mines by moving left or right. The player can x-ray an entire city area at any time. If the scanner encounters a mine signal they must quickly hunt the air mine, and fire when discovered. If they hesitate the city is vaporized. If Flutter Drones are encountered, the player must quickly determine if they intend to attack, and then activate defence shields to protect the scanner. There are 3 levels of difficulty, and the player has minimal energy to finish their mission.

446571.overview: In Sea Search you must find several treasures throughout this aquatic adventure. It will require deep sea diving and a little digging to find them all. You will need to elude several dangers from pirates to man eating sharks or become fish bait.

446575.overview: The player controls a small ship at the bottom of the screen, which moves horizontally and fires vertically upwards. Alien vessels move as a group horizontally across the screen until they reach the edge, move down 1 level, and reverse direction. As they move, aliens fire towards the player. Three barricades offer protection for the player. When all enemy vessels are destroyed, the player moves to a higher challenge, where the enemy vessels start 1 row lower. The player starts with 3 ships, and bonus ships are made available at point thresholds dependent upon skill level. There are 3 levels of difficulty.

446655.overview: The second half of Savage Island, this continues exactly where the other game leaves off. It includes a mysterious code sheet which you will be able to decipher upon completing the game, revealing the ultimate secret of the island.

457835.overview:
School Maze is an adventure game about locating a lost computer tape within a school building.

The player navigates a top-down map of the school, starting by obtaining a hall pass from the school office. Once acquired, the player can explore various rooms, searching for the missing tape.
